components.meaning: jade (king-like form, from 玉)
to seek (phonetic, gives the sound qiú)

compositionNote: Jade (王) shows balls were once precious round stones, while 求 lends the sound qiú.
poem: A king (王) went out to seek (求) some fun,
He chased a BALL (qiú) beneath the sun,
Round and bouncy, jade-bright gleam,
Kick it, throw it, join the team!

components.meaning: to be; right (phonetic hint)
head; page (semantic, related to a heading)

compositionNote: 页 (head/page) shows this is about a heading or title, while 是 contributes a sound close to tí.
poem: Is (是) it right? Turn the page (页) to see,
A tricky TOPIC (tí) waits for thee,
Questions written line by line,
Answer well and you'll be fine!

meanings.def: to jump; to leap; to bounce

components.meaning: foot (semantic, action of the feet)
omen (phonetic, gives the sound tiào)

compositionNote: The foot (足) does the moving while 兆 supplies the sound tiào.
poem: Feet (足) sense an omen (兆), start to spring,
They JUMP (tiào) and leap at anything,
Up and over, quick and light,
Hopping high from morn to night!

components.meaning: originally a picture of a dancer holding streamers
two feet pointing opposite ways (semantic, movement of feet)

compositionNote: The top once pictured a dancer with flowing sleeves; once that shape was borrowed to mean 'not have', 舛 (feet) was added to keep the meaning of dancing.
poem: A dancer twirled with silk in hand,
Two feet (舛) kept time across the land,
Swirl and sway, the DANCE (wǔ) unfolds,
A story that the body holds!

components.meaning: roof (semantic, a house)
first; origin (phonetic, gives the sound wán)

compositionNote: A roof (宀) over 元 suggests a house brought to completion, with 元 also hinting at the sound wán.
poem: Under the roof (宀), from first (元) to end,
The work is FINISHED (wán), time to spend,
Every task now closed and done,
Roof stands proud when day is won!

components.meaning: jade (semantic, toying with a gem)
first; origin (phonetic, gives the sound wán)

compositionNote: Jade (王) suggests fiddling with a gem for amusement, while 元 gives the sound wán.
poem: A prince (王) with jewels, first (元) of all,
Loves to PLAY (wán) and have a ball,
Toys and games from dawn to dark,
Every jade gem sparks a spark!

components.meaning: sun (semantic, time of day)
to avoid (phonetic, gives the sound wǎn)

compositionNote: The sun (日) low in the sky marks evening, while 免 lends the sound wǎn.
poem: The sun (日) tries to avoid (免) the night,
But EVENING (wǎn) comes, dimming light,
Late and slow the day retires,
Stars replace the sun's own fires.

components.meaning: step; to walk (semantic, movement)
master (phonetic, gives a sound close to wǎng)

compositionNote: Walking steps (彳) show motion toward somewhere, while 主 contributes the sound.
poem: Steps (彳) march on, the master's (主) way,
Heading TOWARD (wǎng) the break of day,
Past roads walked and paths ahead,
Onward still, by feet we're led.

meanings.def: to do; to act as; to become

components.meaning: originally a hand leading an elephant, picturing 'to do work'

compositionNote: The simplified form no longer shows its parts clearly; it comes from an old picture of a hand guiding an elephant to work.
poem: A hand once led an elephant near,
To DO (wéi), to act — the sense is clear,
It stands for tasks both big and small,
One little word that means it all.

components.meaning: to lose; to perish (phonetic, gives the sound wàng)
heart (semantic, mental state)

compositionNote: Something lost (亡) from the heart (心) is quite literally forgotten.
poem: Something's lost (亡) inside the heart (心),
Memories that fall apart,
To FORGET (wàng) what once we knew,
Slips away like morning dew.

components.meaning: door (phonetic, gives the sound wèn)
mouth (semantic, speaking)

compositionNote: A mouth (口) at the door (门) calls out to ask something, with 门 also lending the sound.
poem: Knock the door (门), open your mouth (口) wide,
ASK (wèn) a question, step inside,
Curious minds will always seek,
Answers found for those who speak.

components.meaning: a picture of a vine with a melon hanging from it

compositionNote: A single pictograph showing a melon dangling on its curling vine.
poem: A curling vine, a dangling round,
A juicy MELON (guā) on the ground,
Sweet and cool on summer days,
Vines twist round in curly ways.

components.meaning: crossed lines (semantic, a sparse, loose weave)
cloth (semantic, fabric)

compositionNote: Loosely crossed threads (爻) on cloth (巾) picture a sparse weave, extended to mean something rare — hence hoped for.
poem: Threads cross and weave upon the cloth (巾),
A sparse design, both fine and soft,
We HOPE (xī) for dreams that rarely come,
Rare as thread that's finely spun.

meanings.def: to look toward; to gaze into the distance

components.meaning: to lose; gone (phonetic hint, gives the sound wàng)
moon (semantic, gazing at the moon)

compositionNote: Someone gazes up at the moon (月) longing for what is gone (亡), the origin of both 'to gaze' and 'to hope'.
poem: Lost (亡) at night, we watch the moon (月),
And HOPE (wàng) the morning comes real soon,
Gazing far past hill and tree,
Wishing for what eyes can't see.

components.meaning: water (semantic, washing)
first (phonetic, gives the sound xǐ)

compositionNote: Water (氵) does the washing, while 先 lends its sound to xǐ.
poem: Water (氵) flows to go first (先) of all,
To WASH (xǐ) away both dirt and squall,
Scrub your hands and rinse them clean,
Freshest start you've ever seen.

components.meaning: bamboo (semantic, bending like laughter bends the body)
bent over (phonetic-semantic, a person bending)

compositionNote: Bamboo (竹) bending in the wind is likened to a body bent over with laughter (夭).
poem: Bamboo (竹) leans and bends with glee (夭),
We LAUGH (xiào) so hard, we bend our knee,
Giggles rustle just like leaves,
Joy that bamboo swaying weaves.

components.meaning: dear; parent (phonetic, gives the sound xīn)
axe (semantic, cutting fresh wood)

compositionNote: An axe (斤) cutting fresh wood gives the idea of newness, while 亲 lends the sound xīn.
poem: A dear one (亲) chops wood with an axe (斤),
Fresh planks emerge from ancient stacks,
Something NEW (xīn) begins to form,
Bright and different, freshly born.

components.meaning: woman (semantic, ancient clans traced through mothers)
to be born (phonetic-semantic, gives sound and sense of lineage)

compositionNote: A woman (女) giving birth (生) reflects how ancient surnames were originally passed down through mothers' clans.
poem: A woman (女) gives birth (生) to a name,
Passed through lines from whence they came,
Your SURNAME (xìng) tells your family tree,
Roots that trace through history.

components.meaning: person (semantic)
tree (semantic)

compositionNote: A person (亻) leaning against a tree (木) pictures the very act of resting.
poem: A person (亻) leans against a tree (木),
Taking time to REST (xiū) so free,
Shade above and grass below,
Napping where the breezes blow.

components.meaning: nose (semantic, originally a picture of a nose, source of breath)
heart (semantic)

compositionNote: Breath from the nose (自) reaching the heart (心) pictures breathing and, by extension, resting.
poem: The nose (自) breathes deep, the heart (心) beats slow,
A quiet BREATH (xī) begins to flow,
Rest a while and catch your air,
Peaceful moments everywhere.

components.meaning: rain (semantic, precipitation)
a hand or broom (originally used to sweep snow, semantic hint)

compositionNote: Rain (雨) that turns cold falls as snow, with the lower part once picturing a hand sweeping it away.
poem: Rain (雨) turns cold, a hand (彐) will sweep,
White SNOW (xuě) falls in drifts so deep,
Flakes come dancing from the sky,
Blanket fields as winter's nigh.

components.meaning: an accomplished man (phonetic, gives a sound close to yán)
head (semantic, the face)

compositionNote: 页 (head) points to the face, whose expression and hue give this character its meanings of face and color; 彦 lends the sound.
poem: A noble man (彦) shows his head (页) with pride,
His COLORFUL (yán) face he can't hide,
Every hue upon his cheek,
Tells the story words can't speak.

components.meaning: originally two figures side by side, picturing a facial expression or complexion

compositionNote: An old picture of a person's complexion or mood, later generalized to mean 'color'.
poem: Two figures bend in shifting hue,
A COLOR (sè) shows a mood or two,
Red for joy and blue for calm,
Every shade an ancient charm.

components.meaning: eye (semantic, a picture of an eye)
to stop; firm (phonetic, gives the sound yǎn)

compositionNote: 目 (eye) carries the meaning, while 艮 supplies the sound yǎn.
poem: An eye (目) stands firm and will not budge (艮),
The EYE (yǎn) that watches, does not fudge,
Windows to the soul they say,
Seeing all both night and day.

components.meaning: eye (semantic)
blue-green (phonetic, gives the sound jīng)

compositionNote: 目 (eye) gives the meaning of eyeball, while 青 lends the sound jīng.
poem: An eye (目) so bright, like green-blue skies (青),
The EYEBALL (jīng) sparkles, never lies,
Paired with 眼 to make a stare,
Dot the dragon's eye with care.

components.meaning: a picture of a sheep's head with curving horns

compositionNote: A pictograph of a sheep's head, seen from the front with its curved horns.
poem: Two curving horns upon a head,
A woolly SHEEP (yáng) in pasture led,
Baa and graze from morn to dusk,
Fluffy white in fields of musk.

components.meaning: a picture of a cross-section of meat with muscle lines

compositionNote: A pictograph showing a slice of meat with the lines of its muscle or ribs.
poem: A slice with lines like ribs inside,
Fresh MEAT (ròu) upon the chopping side,
Sizzle, grill it, stew it too,
Dinner's ready, made for you.

components.meaning: grass (semantic, medicinal herbs)
to agree; approximately (phonetic, gives the sound yào)

compositionNote: Herbs (艹) form the basis of medicine, while 约 lends its sound to yào.
poem: Herbs (艹) agreed upon (约) with care,
Brewed as MEDICINE (yào) to share,
Bitter sips to make you well,
Nature's cure in leaf and shell.

components.meaning: originally a picture of a curling snake or ladle, later borrowed as a grammar word

compositionNote: An ancient pictograph whose original picture was borrowed purely for its sound to write the grammatical word 'also'.
poem: A curling snake once slid this way,
Now means 'ALSO' (yě) in what we say,
Me too, you too, and him as well,
A tiny word with much to tell.

components.meaning: sound (semantic, a sound from within)
heart (semantic, feeling and thought)

compositionNote: A sound (音) rising from the heart (心) captures an inner meaning or intention.
poem: A sound (音) rings out straight from the heart (心),
An IDEA (yì) starts to take its part,
Meaning hidden, feeling deep,
Thoughts the mind will always keep.

components.meaning: field-like shape, actually a simplified form of 囟 (skull/fontanelle)
heart (semantic)

compositionNote: The top part looks like a field (田) but is really a worn-down form of 囟 (the skull), combined with 心 (heart) to represent thinking with mind and heart together.
poem: The brain (囟, like a field 田) and heart (心) combine,
To THINK (sī) and ponder, thoughts align,
Ideas grow like crops in rows,
Wisdom blooms where thinking grows.

meanings.def: yin (the shady, feminine principle, opposite of yang)

components.meaning: mound; hill (semantic, the shady side of a hill)
moon (semantic, associated with darkness and yin)

compositionNote: The shady side of a hill (阝) paired with the moon (月) pictures shade, cloudiness, and the yin principle.
poem: The shady mound (阝), the pale moon's (月) glow,
OVERCAST (yīn) skies, the sun lies low,
Yin and shadow, dim and cool,
Nature's balance, nature's rule.

components.meaning: enclosure (semantic, a mat or boundary)
big; a person (semantic, a person resting on a mat)

compositionNote: A person (大) resting inside an enclosure or mat (囗) originally meant 'to rely on', which extended to mean the cause one relies on.
poem: A person (大) rests inside a mat (囗),
BECAUSE (yīn) of comfort found in that,
Every cause has its own seed,
Reasons planted, thoughts proceed.

components.meaning: water (semantic)
forever (phonetic, gives the sound yǒng, originally a picture of a long flowing stream)

compositionNote: Water (氵) plus 永, which originally pictured a long branching stream, together give 'to swim'.
poem: Water (氵) flows on forever (永) still,
We SWIM (yǒng) with strokes and steady will,
Kick and glide beneath the waves,
Forever flowing, water's ways.

components.meaning: hand (semantic, a hand helping)
mouth (semantic, feeding oneself)

compositionNote: A hand (又) helping the mouth (口) reflects that most people use their right hand to eat, giving 'right side' its meaning.
poem: A hand (又) once helped to feed the mouth (口),
The RIGHT (yòu) side, strong from north to south,
Most of us reach with this same hand,
The right side helps us understand.

components.meaning: a picture of a fish with head, body, and tail

compositionNote: A pictograph of a fish, viewed from the side with its head, scaled body, and tail.
poem: A fish's fins, a fish's tail,
Swimming fast, it will not fail,
FISH (yú) that swim in streams and seas,
Gliding past with silver ease.
